identityTest.stableIdentity: A standing authorization is independently identifiable only when it persists beyond one decision occurrence with its own holder, scope, validity, renewal and revocation lifecycle.
identityTest.versionIdentity: Scope, conditions, accountable authority, validity or safeguards change only through a successor instrument or revision.

references.purpose: Decision options, criteria, conditions and rationale
Issued record and immutable instrument evidence

invariants: Independent identity requires persistence beyond one issued decision record.
Every authorization names accountable authority, holder, scope, conditions and validity.
Expired, revoked or suspended authorization is not effective.
Context or subject changes require scope proof, successor authorization or explicit non-applicability.
Issued records remain immutable and corrections are additive.
Authorization conditions never overwrite cited assessment or evaluation evidence.
Decision rationale, authorized act and issued instrument retain separate mastership.
Renewal creates a governed successor or revision with preserved history.
Revocation records actor, authority, time and reason.
Standing authorization never owns deployment or endpoint runtime lifecycle.
A high score cannot widen authorization scope.
Retired identifiers and revisions remain resolvable and are never recycled.
holds: Candidate is conditional on a lifecycle beyond one issued record.
Registry allocation is pending and no identifier may be guessed.
Decision-triad ownership and frozen deployment authority require reconciliation.
Frozen audit, relation approvals and fixtures remain pending.
